subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: The original 'No-Detention Policy' under the RTE Act, 2009 (which prohibited failing/holding back students up to Class 8), was significantly amended in 2019 to allow states to:

options.option_text: Conduct regular examinations at the end of Class 5 and Class 8, holding back students who fail even after a re-examination opportunity
Permanently expel students who fail any class
Make examinations compulsory from Class 1 onward

explanation: The 2019 RTE Amendment gave states the option to detain students in Class 5 and/or Class 8 if they fail a year-end exam and a subsequent re-examination, reversing the strict blanket no-detention rule that had drawn criticism for reducing accountability for learning outcomes.
